survivingClaim: No statement about zeros of zeta; precise obstruction stands. (1) TN1 = zeta(s)(1+q^(3/4-s)) is integer-frequency, multiplicative, non-negative, single pole at 1, zeros on Re s=3/4, lacks FE. (2) HQ2 = zeta(s)(1+eps u^2/(1-u)^4), u=q^(1/2-s), has zeta's exact functional equation, integer frequencies, multiplicative coefficients >=1, zeros at distance eps^(1/4)/(sqrt2 log q)(1+O(sqrt eps)) from the line, and an order-4 pole at s=1/2: ordinary multiplicativity replaces neither the FE clause nor the pole clause of Hamburger/Theorem P. (3) Lemma Q: a pole-free symmetric one-base multiplier is 1 (Liouville; no multiplicativity). (4) Proposition F: members with zeta's coefficients for n<q, exact FE, multiplicative non-negative coefficients, within delta of zeta on Re s>=2, vanish on Re s=3/4. (5) Among the listed relations only a(pn)=a(n) (definition) and J=1 (target) exclude every control. Statements that ZQ, NR-q, Proposition W twin pass multiplicativity are by convention; Proposition D (c) needs repair. One referee holds with corrections; elementary; no ball arithmetic.

lesson: Rigidity on file is linear algebra in the coefficient measure (FE, integrality and the pole clause intersect in a line); multiplicativity is linear in a different coordinate (log G) and is never needed. The one clause that completes the identification, analyticity on the critical line, is the only one not stated right of 1. In the coefficient topology zeros are discontinuous even inside {FE, INT, MULT, N>=0}. Do not look for a control that fails through multiplicativity inside an exact relation.
